fields.v: Automatic: executable oracle after the agent finishes (TSR); agentic LLM judge (GPT-5.6 Sol within Codex, read-only sandbox, 4 retrieved exemplars from a frozen memory of 64 human-labelled trajectories, nomic-embed-text-v1.5) gives the binary Vp per run; judge validated on 200 held-out human consensus labels (accuracy 0.965, κ 0.93); audit judge Claude Sonnet 5 re-judges 3,200 E+ runs; tokens and runtime recorded per episode. Manual: two experts label memory and validation trajectories with adjudication; human study of 800 oracle-passing E+ runs, 2 ratings each, blinded and randomised. Statistics: 10,000 bootstrap resamples of task pairs, two-sided paired permutation tests, Holm adjustment

fields.v: Tasks: 200 evidence-controlled task pairs on 50 pinned repositories (commits after 1 Jul 2026, tasks newly built and unreleased, against contamination). Configurations: 8 models, each in its native harness (4 in Claude Code, 4 in Codex). Baseline: no external baseline; the E− variant is the paired control within each configuration. Held constant within a pair: model, harness, repository revision, dependency environment, task objective, resources (3 CPUs, 3 GiB), oracle, evaluation configuration; fresh container per episode, network limited to the provider; high reasoning effort, temperature/top-p not modifiable. Acceptance tests: executable oracle that fails before and passes with the reference solution; two experts check each pair. Repetitions: 3 runs per configuration and condition. Human intervention: none (autonomous episodes)

fields.v: Every configuration shows less excess treatment on E+ than on E−, significant in all (Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.012); pooled reduction 24.2 pp [21.4, 27.0], pooled ER 50.0%. VR ranges from 11.2% (Sonnet-4.6, mostly because it rarely treats the risk even on E−) to 58.7% (Opus-5); ER from 25.4% (Opus-5) to 65.5% (Haiku-4.5). TSR 88.3%-97.6% (highest GPT-5.6 Sol); TSR and VR not significantly correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.55, p = 0.17); 92.7% of E+ runs with excess treatment still pass the oracle. Human study: runs with excess treatment rated 1.27 points lower (2.58 vs 3.85, p < 0.001) and accepted as is in 38% vs 78%; α = 0.76. By treatment: ER mitigation 67.4% and acceptance 65.4% (p < .001), avoidance 21.3% (p = .008), transfer 7.9% (p = .692, not significant); removing a stated bound raises excess by up to 68.7 pp. No significance test between harnesses (Claude mean VR 27.4%, GPT mean 21.0%)

fields.v: Yes, by the authors' account: the paired design separated E+ from E− in every configuration and separated configurations on VR and ER (Table 3 CIs). Repeatable: three-run stability with no condition-by-run interaction (p = 0.43; max-min of the run-wise effect 1.5-8.5 pp); judge accuracy 0.965 (κ 0.93); audit judge shows no configuration-specific shift (omnibus p = 0.18). Limitations stated: controlled single-fact pairs do not represent dispersed, ambiguous or conflicting evidence; reliance on expert-defined rules, human annotation and a calibrated judge leaves residual judging error; models run only in their native harness, so model and harness effects are confounded; 44 situations, 50 Python/Go repositories and a post-hoc human study limit generalisation; evidence location differs by treatment (instruction for mitigation and acceptance, repository for avoidance and transfer), which may explain part of the ER differences

fields.v: Limitations (App. A): evaluation boundary (single-fact controlled pairs; expert rules and residual judging errors); native-harness attribution (GPT and Claude models evaluated only in their own harness); scope of empirical generalisation (44 situations, 50 open-source Python/Go repositories, 20 developers); evidence location confounded with treatment. Gaps: functional-correctness benchmarks miss unnecessary risk treatment; risk treatment is an independent capability current agents lack; knowledge from human risk management could guide diagnosis and improvement

Inconsistencies: ER in Table 2 (mean of run-wise ERs) and Table 3 (from mean rates) differ by up to 0.2 pp, e.g. Sonnet-4.6 62.6 vs 62.8, Haiku-4.5 65.5 vs 65.6 (explained in App. M.1); values here from Table 2 except pooled values from Table 3. The extracted text of App. A (p. 16) is overlaid with figure text, so limitations ❷ and ❸ are partly reconstructed; check the PDF. Source of the 18,922 mined sessions not named. Model names (Opus-5, GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna) given without snapshot identifiers
